page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Margin notes in the left margin: "An. M.cccc. XCIII." beside the second paragraph, and "Otto Langius legatus Cæsaris in Frisia" beside the line "LANGIUS".

main_text.p: HARINGÆO factionis principe, ad arbitrium victorum conditiones accepere. Iurarunt, fœ-deri Oftergoo non se semet oppositurus, nec impedimento iis futuros, si qui deinceps aut Oftergoi aut VVestergoi accedere eidem velent: nullum jus imperiumve in universam Oftergoam, aut ullam eius partem sibi arro-gaturos, ablata redditurosque in integrum restituturos, controversiam cum Galamæis arbitrio Groningensium submissuros: Groningen-genses in persequendis iniuriis contra VVestergoos hac pactione non comprehensos non impedituros: è sociis in has leges peccanti nemini patrocinaturos: detrimenta, impen-dia, molestias belli Groningani & Oftergois XVII millib. aureorum Rhenens. & quingentis spacio 1x mensium terminis pensionibus farturos. Deniq; alia obligandæ fidei vincula gravia & asperæ adjuncta: quæ in historia ex-pono. Tum consternatis totius factionis ad-versæ animis, quotquot eius in Oftergoa supe-rerant, viri nobiles, quos hactenus pertinacia siverat[?] accedere, eidem fœderi Oftergoo accefferunt.

In hoc rerum statu, cum omnia ad amplian-dos fœderis huiusce fines spectare viderentur, venit in Frisiam legatus Cæsaris Friderici OTTO Otto Langius legatus Cæsaris in FrisiaLANGIUS canonicus Moguntinus, ut Frisiorum dissidia componeret. Cuius adventu respi-rantes Scaringi (horum enim precibus data legati missio erat) animos rursum extulere, tur-basq; dedere fœderatis. Nec multo post è vita decessit Fridericus III imperator, ad quem reverterat.

page.notes: Printed "fiverat" in the first paragraph is probably "siverat" (sinerat) and is marked [?]. "supe-rerant" at the line break is uncertain and may be "superarant"; the second part is unclear. The left-margin note "Ann. M.cccc. XCIII." is transcribed as printed (OCR: "XGIII"). Long s is rendered as s throughout. The head "HARINGÆO" is set in small capitals and is treated as the start of a continued paragraph.
